# Knowledge-Core: Conventions

## Errors

Go constructors validate required dependencies and return `(T, error)`. Errors add operation context, keep the cause with `%w`, and use `errors.Is` / `errors.As`. Cross-boundary errors use `pkg/error` code/key/kind. Do not use `Must*`, panic for business failure, or `os.Exit` outside the process entrypoint.

## Logging and telemetry

Propagate `context.Context`, deadlines, request IDs, and W3C trace end to end. Metric labels and span attributes stay on route templates, RPC methods, status codes, stable business codes, and dependency names. Knowledge and Attachment worker empty-claim probes use `trace.Suppress` so idle SQL does not export orphan roots; claimed work uses a short unsuppressed span. GetConsumerState treats a missing namespace as DesiredRevision=0 idle state, not NotFound.

## Tests

Tests stay close to implementation and cover success, edges, dependency failure, error mapping, cleanup/rollback, and deterministic concurrent behavior. Rust requires rustfmt, clippy `-D warnings`, and cargo deny.

## Secrets and layout

Repository text uses LF except `.bat` / `.cmd`. Module and directory ownership lives in `conventions.code-layout`, not architecture.

## 4. Repository modules

```text
pkg/                          Cross-service shared capability; must not depend back on services
  app/                        Process lifecycle and component orchestration
  auth/                       Ed25519 JWT wire contract
  codec/json/                 Strict HTTP JSON codec
  error/                      Stable errors, Kitex/Hertz mapping, RFC 9457
  option/                     Reusable configuration models
  log / trace / metrics / health / metadata /
  postgres / redis / nats /
  circuit/                    Outbound RPC consecutive-failure circuit
  configcenter/               Nacos ApplicationConfig envelope
  transport/                  Hertz admin and Kitex client adapters

services/<go-service>/
  main.go                     Only create and execute the application command
  spec.go                     Only declare pkg/app.Spec
  etc/config.yaml             Service-private non-sensitive static config
  internal/config/            Config loading and dynamic revision
  internal/context/           Explicit ServiceContext assembly
  internal/domain|logic|repository|transport|client|worker/

services/collaboration/
  src/actor.rs                Document actor: commit before apply/broadcast
  src/websocket.rs            Axum WebSocket, y-sync, awareness
  src/rpc/                    Volo server/client, static DNS, mTLS, circuit
  src/storage/                SQLx PostgreSQL and migrations
  src/worker.rs               Projection, snapshot, auto version, outbox, invalidation
  src/ticket.rs / routing.rs  One-time ticket and instance stickiness
  src/generated/              Generator-owned; do not hand-edit
  interop/                    Node/Yjs/y-prosemirror fixtures; not in production images

idl/http/v1                   Public HTTP contract source
idl/rpc/v1                    Internal Thrift contract source
kitex_gen/                    Go generated code, owned by the generator
scripts/generated-files.txt   Sole generated-file ownership list
deploy/<service>/{base,overlay/dev}  Per-service Kustomize
docker/                       Local infrastructure and service images
docs/                         Verified design
```

Go service assembly direction is fixed:

```text
main/spec -> internal/config -> internal/context -> domain / logic / repository / transport
```

Layer responsibilities:

- `domain`: domain objects and validation.
- `model`: GORM persistence models only; do not leak across unrelated boundaries.
- `logic`: organized by use case; depends on small in-service interfaces.
- `repository`: persistence, transactions, and storage error mapping.
- `transport`: protocol validation, orchestration, and safe error mapping; does not hold domain rules.
- `ServiceContext`: holds service dependencies explicitly. `pkg/app.Runtime` owns process-level logging, tracing, health, metrics, components, and cleanup; it is not a service locator.

<!-- fact:conventions.code-layout status:verified sources:filesystem:top-level-directories, user-confirmed, user-confirmed-en-locale-source, user-confirmed-schema-v2-rerecord -->

Secrets may be injected only from environment variables, Kubernetes Secrets, or SOPS-encrypted GitOps manifests. Sensitive values must not be stored in plaintext in source, configuration, logs, metrics, trace spans, or release metadata.
